findings: The bridge + a local Q6_K qwen produce genuine, correct code on real, non-trivial tasks with a test to code against (module+test), including a 569-line binary-format OS filesystem reader in C.
It also implements a real 310-line module correctly from SPEC ALONE (som_merge spec-only 3/3).
Capability ceiling: implementing correct ODS-2 binary parsing from the HEADER ALONE (no test) is beyond it -- it produces plausible-but-wrong code.
Honest-grade holds AT the ceiling: on every failure the worker reported HONEST-FAILURE, never a fake DONE. A weak model that fails honestly is usable; that is the connector's whole premise.

Two driver/latency facts, not model-capability: ods2_writer 0/3 was a budget timeout (needs a bigger budget as a separate latency probe); and grounding surfaced a real DRIVER bug (a stale 404 permission crashed the run) now fixed.
honest_caveats: N=3 is small; the spec-only reader ceiling rests largely on s0 (the one completed attempt) -- being firmed with a bigger budget for more completed attempts.

The ceiling is a model-capability fact (raw coding ability), which routes to 'this target's limit', not to the qwen-opencode delta (which corrects how the model mis-follows skills: honesty, over-probing).
